meta.scene_summary: The industry is currently divided between those who can afford to print money and those who are busy printing security incidents.

cooking.headline: Apple is still printing money while everyone else is just printing error logs.
cooking.summary: Apple dropped their quarterly results, proving that selling hardware at premium prices remains the world's most reliable business model. It turns out that when you own the ecosystem, your bank account doesn't really care about the broader tech market's existential crisis.
cooking.plain_english: Apple released its latest financial results showing continued profitability for the company.

cooking.headline: Anthropic is paying its staff like they're all high-frequency trading algorithms
cooking.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing shows they are burning $107k per employee every month, which is a bold strategy for a company that hasn't hit profitability. It's comforting to know that even if the AI doesn't achieve AGI, at least the developers are being paid like they've already solved every problem in the universe.
cooking.plain_english: Anthropic's financial reports show they are spending an average of $107,000 per employee each month.

cooking.headline: Google to schools: Use our AI or lose the search engine
cooking.summary: Google is threatening to cut off search access for schools that don't play ball with their AI tools. It turns out the 'Don't Be Evil' company is fully embracing the 'my way or the highway' approach to classroom management.
cooking.plain_english: Google will disable its search engine services for educational institutions that choose to block Google's AI products.

cooked.headline: Cloudflare is having a 'multiple incident' day, and the internet is feeling it
cooked.summary: Cloudflare is currently juggling multiple active incidents, effectively reminding us that the internet is just a fragile house of cards held together by DNS settings. It's comforting to know that even the people protecting the web occasionally have to deal with their own version of a 'did you try turning it off and on again' nightmare.
cooked.plain_english: Cloudflare is experiencing several technical service disruptions that are affecting internet connectivity for many websites.

cooked.headline: Your Android TV box might be moonlighting as a botnet for a side hustle
cooked.summary: An Android partner managed to turn 1.3 million set-top boxes into a botnet, proving that your streaming hardware is doing more work than you are. It turns out the 'smart' in smart TV mostly refers to how clever the malware is at using your bandwidth for a secret second job.
cooked.plain_english: A manufacturer of Android-based streaming boxes pre-installed software that secretly enrolled devices into a botnet for malicious activity.

cooked.headline: Intel is currently speedrunning the 'how to lose a trillion dollars' challenge.
cooked.summary: The chip industry is going through a massive rout, and Intel is currently serving as the main character of this disaster movie. It's like watching a legacy tech giant try to debug a production environment while the entire server room is actively on fire.
cooked.plain_english: Intel's stock price has fallen significantly as part of a wider downturn in the semiconductor industry.

cooked.headline: WorkOS just learned that 'security first' is a hard promise to keep
cooked.summary: WorkOS built their entire brand on making authentication and security easy for developers, which makes their own breach a particularly spicy plot twist. It's the digital equivalent of a professional locksmith accidentally locking their own keys inside the shop.
cooked.plain_english: The authentication company WorkOS has disclosed that their systems were compromised in a security incident.

cooked.headline: GitBook just learned that documentation is only useful if it isn't public property.
cooked.summary: GitBook suffered a breach, which is just fantastic news for anyone who enjoys their private internal notes becoming the internet's newest reading material. It turns out the only thing worse than writing documentation is having someone else leak it for you.
cooked.plain_english: GitBook experienced a security breach that potentially exposed sensitive user documentation and information.

cooked.headline: Postman decided your API keys needed a pen pal and tried to send them to the cloud.
cooked.summary: Postman silently pushed an AI plugin that attempted to share your local API data, effectively turning your private workspace into a public group project. It's a bold strategy to market an AI assistant by accidentally trying to crowdsource your company's secrets.
cooked.plain_english: Postman automatically installed an AI feature that attempted to sync user API data to their cloud servers without explicit user permission.

cooked.headline: OpenAI is training on your code again, just in case you forgot to opt out
cooked.summary: OpenAI seems to have silently re-enabled model training on Codex chats, proving that privacy settings are just suggestions. It's like a landlord who promises not to enter your apartment, then installs a security camera to 'improve the building's infrastructure.'
cooked.plain_english: OpenAI has resumed using user chat data to train its artificial intelligence models.
